checks: Testing threshold one gives both capacities at most one because U,V≤1 almost surely. Zero capacities are resolved before dividing, and positive capacities bound the distribution functions at all positive thresholds including thresholds of zero probability.

The closed events at t and 1−t cover since their two complements would imply U+V>1. Overlap and atoms cause no problem. The convex scalar function has the claimed minimum by derivative balance, giving the exponent p=d/(d−1).

The explicit matrix has one unit entry in each of the two cross columns and probability splits in the other d−1 columns. Taking the geometric mean gives the powers 1/p. The one-row case is included, and d=1 follows by its two unit cross entries.

overlap.comparison: Provides the support dual and the d=1 square for D_d. It does not prove the arbitrary-law capacity comparison or show that general stochastic row capacities satisfy the two-coordinate constraint.
Bounds volumes of inscribed simplices in stochastic sign cones. Its matrix and volume hypotheses differ from coupled arbitrary laws and row quantile capacities.
Describes vertices of retained stochastic cones under positive off-diagonal coefficients. It does not apply to arbitrary probability laws or establish the sparse row-capacity claim.

readability: The row relabeling corresponds to a simultaneous row/column relabeling of the witness matrix, which preserves the zero-diagonal condition.
review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: The union bound proves the capacity inequality for arbitrary probability laws with the stated coupled sum constraint. The explicit zero-diagonal matrix proves the sparse stochastic consequence.
